body:
Here is the exact local fix I had been carrying, plus the reasoning behind it.

What I changed locally in `tools/transcription_tools.py`:

```python
try:
    segments, info = _local_model.transcribe(file_path, **transcribe_kwargs)
except RuntimeError as e:
    error_text = str(e)
    if "libcublas.so" not in error_text and "cublas" not in error_text.lower():
        raise
    logger.warning(
        "faster-whisper GPU runtime unavailable (%s); retrying on CPU int8",
        error_text,
    )
    _local_model = WhisperModel(model_name, device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
    _local_model_name = f"{model_name}:cpu-int8"
    segments, info = _local_model.transcribe(file_path, **transcribe_kwargs)
```

Why I changed it this way:

1. The existing local STT path tries `WhisperModel(..., device="auto", compute_type="auto")` first, which is reasonable.
2. In some environments, that succeeds far enough to initialize the model path, but transcription then fails at runtime because the CUDA / cuBLAS libraries are not actually usable at execution time.
3. In that situation, failing outright seemed unnecessarily harsh, because CPU inference is still a viable fallback.
4. I intentionally limited the fallback to cuBLAS-related runtime failures only, so unrelated `RuntimeError`s still surface normally instead of being silently masked.

What problem this solved for me:

- Before the patch: local STT could hard-fail on a GPU runtime/library problem even though CPU transcription would have worked.
- After the patch: Hermes still tries the faster path first, but if the failure is specifically a cuBLAS runtime issue, it degrades gracefully to CPU int8 and transcription completes.

So the practical goal was not to change the preferred execution path, but to make local STT more robust when GPU support is only partially available.

If there is already a preferred upstream way to handle this class of failure, I would be happy to switch to that instead.
Related to #13568 (same fallback feature) and PR #13571 (caches CPU fallback). Also see #17559 for Blackwell-specific cuBLAS variant.

Thanks for the detailed write-up and for sharing the exact patch you were carrying — this is a great bug report.

This is an automated hermes-sweeper review.

The fallback you proposed is fully implemented on `main` as of commit [`4350668`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/4350668ae49c903640179ebdaa99f59687ff951c):

- **`_load_local_whisper_model()`** (`tools/transcription_tools.py` ~line 350): tries `device="auto"`, catches CUDA library load errors via `_looks_like_cuda_lib_error()`, falls back to `device="cpu", compute_type="int8"`.
- **`_transcribe_local()`** (~line 406): additionally wraps `transcribe()` itself — evicts the broken cached model, reloads on CPU+int8, retries once. This handles the exact case you described where the model loads fine but `transcribe()` fails at first dlopen.
- The `_CUDA_LIB_ERROR_MARKERS` list includes `"libcublas"`, `"libcudnn"`, `"libcudart"`, `"cannot be loaded"`, `"no CUDA-capable device"`, and driver-mismatch strings — matching your own design of limiting fallback to cuBLAS-related failures only.

Linked issue #2885 (which you noted as a potential duplicate) was also closed once this fix landed. Your patch and the upstream implementation are functionally equivalent — you can drop your local modification and `hermes update` will carry the fix going forward.
